Adoption Scam

By: Sasha Schwendenwein | Paid

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
You've struggled to conceive, and so you turn to adoption, but the person you've trust with finding your bundle of joy seems a likely conwoman

Unique Selling Point:
We have this story exclusively. Letitia van den Berg, has scammed 10 couple that we are aware of as a "Professional Social worker & Adoption Specialist (Practice Nr: 890000372846 & Reg Nr: 10-19899) as she states on her FB account.

This adoption worker asks couples for money after she has 'matched' you with a Mom whom wants to give her baby up for adoption.

However in all 10 our cases we are not even sure if there was a baby etc.

THE ONLY ISSUE IS THAT WE NEED TO WAIT FOR THURSDAY TO SEE WHAT HAPPEND WITH SHANNON'S ADOPTION. She found a child without Letitia and need's her to go to court and get the court order for the adoption - then her lawyers and her will come on board. Shannon and Sonia were both given the same scan pictures of the same baby! And then Sonia was told the mother no longer wanted to give the child up for adoption.





Summary:
Couples Info

Irene – 072 606 0991 - was told twice her baby had died, but has proof that they didn't exist

Elsa – 071 681 1254 has proof her 'baby' was also offered to others

Lynn – 076 068 7667 - her baby "died" - has proof it doesn't exist

Sonika – 076 400 2456 etc

Wynand – 082 451 1009

Carmen – 072 265 9596

Christiaan – 082 773 3324 - he and his husband were told the baby and mother died, and then Irene called the church where the "service" was supposedly held and the church said there was NO such service.

Liezl – 061 548 6423

Shannon – 079 898 7824 - court case

Sonia – 082 495 3841

Maria – 073 564 6622



At least 3 of the couples will appear on camera. They have already experienced so much pain and suffering from not being able to naturally fall pregnant and then this woman has come along and scammed them. They all paid different amounts but roughly 30k each.





Further information:
We know where Letitia works from and can go catch her.

We would need to interview the department of social development about the adoption process etc.

No one had received a death certificate, or any proof that their child existed except for sonia and shannon's case. But that's because shannon found the baby. No one has got their money back.

Rental car if we need to go to pretoria for the day

Script:


For many couples, welcoming a bundle of joy into their family is a dream, but conceiving isn’t guaranteed.
Sonia: We had tried to have children naturally and with IVF, it was a period of about seven years.
Eventually Sonia and Werner Leithgob tried another route - adopting a little girl.
Sonia: We essentially went to court, we signed documents, and we brought the baby home with us.
Last year when they wanted to adopt again, they discovered a woman on Facebook who is a professional social worker and adoption specialist: Hyletta Letitia van den Berg.
Sonia: She's very active and she was also in our area. So we made an appointment to go and see her
And then the wait began, while Van den Berg supposedly began to get their paperwork in order.
Sonia: It was in August 2021 out of the blue she sent my husband a message telling him a birth family has selected you to be the parents of their baby. The birth mom is still pregnant and giving birth, possibly within a month or so
Masa: You were promised the baby even before the baby was born?
Sonia: We were promised the baby a month before the baby was born.
LINK: YOU CAN NEVER PROMISE A BABY BEFORE IT’S BORN - IT’S ILLEGAL. THE CHILDREN’S ACT MAKES IT CLEAR THAT ONLY ONCE THE BABY HAS BEEN DECLARED ADOPTABLE CAN THE PROCESS BEGIN.
VO: That's because the biological parents still have up to 90 days after the birth to change their minds about adoption. In that time the child is placed in temporary care. Statistically there are fewer white babies up for adoption in South Africa, which means long waiting lists.

Among the waiting are Irene and Maco Engelbrecht - clients of Van den Berg since 2016. She offered them two babies before they were born.
Irene: In 2020, she let us know that baby was born dead. We did ask Letitia for death certificates on that baby and she never supplied it to us.

VO: Van den Berg then offered them another baby.

Irene: She said she's got a mummy and the mommy’s pregnant, that she needs to take the baby for scans, etc., and that we must pay 15,000 rand.

That was a birthing fee, bringing the Engelbrechts’ payments to Van den Berg to R40,000. Sonia was also asked for a R17,000 birthing fee. Van den Berg asked both for a large sum, despite the fact that no one should profit from an adoption.
Masa: So if you didn't pay this fee, you lose out on the opportunity?
Sonia: I assume so, because she did say we have to let her know whether we’re interested or not.
Sonia: When the baby was born, Letitia sent us a message with a photograph of the baby. We started getting the baby room ready. We started receiving Christmas presents for the new baby. We told our little girl that she's going to have a baby sister Millie Rose.
The family believed their baby would be home for Christmas.
Sonia: Then we got a voice message from Letitia on Christmas Eve, informing us that, unfortunately, the mom had changed her mind.
Hulle het besluit dat hulle regtig net nie kans sien om voort te gaan met die anneming nie.
They’ve decided that they really just don’t think it’s possible to continue with the adoption.
Hulle het reeds die toestemming tot aaneming teruggetrek.
They have already withdrawn the consent to adoption.

Sonia: Our five year old little girl is waiting for her baby sister. And we had to find the courage to then tell her almost immediately she stopped talking about her baby sister. (move down rest)
We found another nine couples who said they were promised a baby before it was born - some paid significant fees, but never received a child. They were left questioning several of Van Den Berg’s stories - and so did we.
Sonia: We saw how active Letitia was on Facebook. We saw photos of all the moms receiving their new babies, the families getting new babies. And I believe that our baby was given up for adoption but had been given to another family.
We discovered a shocking truth - that multiple couples were offered this particular baby.
Sonia, your suspicions were spot on. We were able to confirm that. How does that make you feel?
Sonia: I just keep thinking about my little girl, my five year old. She didn't get her baby sister. I mean, I'm glad the baby's with another loving family, at least. But I'm heartbroken.
Irene was also suspicious of Van den Berg's stories around the second baby.
She told us that while mummy gave birth she passed away. So obviously that hit us quite hecticly because Mummy's baby girl is born with a lot of complications, according to Letitia.
Irene called up the doctor.
Then that doctor said to me, There is no mummy that passed away in that week and there is no baby with all the health complications that Letitia says.
What happens when you come home and you walk into that room that you had prepared for a baby?
You close the room and then you just don’t go into the room for a few months and it is heartsore … it’s a heartsore journey for all the families.
LINK: THE DEPARTMENT OF SOCIAL DEVELOPMENT SAYS IT DOESN’T REGULATE PRIVATE SOCIAL WORKERS, SO IT REFERRED US TO THE SOUTH AFRICAN COUNCIL OF SOCIAL SERVICE PROFESSIONS.
Hitler: Our mandate is to regulate social service professionals including their professional conduct.
Hitler Sekhitla is head of investigations.
Masa: Let's talk about the law. Should a social worker be promising prospective parents a baby even before they're born?
Hitler: That's unacceptable. That's not allowed. And that kind of conduct constitutes unprofessional conduct.
It turns out that Van den berg is already undergoing a disciplinary process at the council on another case - and more are pending.
Hitler: There are new complaints that we just received. The allegations are shocking and it appears there’s a particular trend.
We discovered a disturbing trend - a decade ago Van den Berg worked for another private adoption agency called PROCARE…there her employment ended in multiple fraud and theft charges.
Elsabe: Letitia was one of our associates since 2007, up until 2013. We trained her to do adoptions
PROCARE CEO Elsabe Engelbrecht says Van Den Berg illegally doctored Procare invoices.
Elsabe: She allegedly defrauded us and we discovered that she would put her name and her banking details and then also the name of Procare so people can think it was Procare that sent this document, it was over a million.
Over a million?
Ja, but the case against her at the moment is for about 600,000 that they got affidavits from.
That case is in court and Van den Berg is on trial for 107 charges relating to fraud and theft.
Masa: What else did you find out in the interim from the adoptive parents?
Elsabe: The stories that some of the adoptive parents told us were just heartbreaking, things like she couldn't, you know, place the baby because the baby died.
Masa: Yeah. We heard that one a lot, too.
Masa: Knowing everything that we know now, including the 107 charges of adoption fraud. Can we look forward to her being suspended following this?
Hitler: Indeed. That's a matter that we need to consider as a matter of urgency.
Letitia: Hello?
Masa: Hi, is this Letitia?
Letitia: Yes
VO: We called Van den Berg to ask for an interview.

Letitia: Sjoe ok, that is quite serious allegations and I can promise you that that’s not the case, um, yes, no so yes it’s fine 11 o’clock on Wednesday I will definitely be available.
MASA: After agreeing to an interview with us Letitia van den Berg asked us for the details of the people who had complained, so we gave her those details so that she could be prepared for the interview. Shortly afterwards she sent us a text message to say that she’s feeling ill and will no longer be talking to us.
VO: She then removed some of the parents from her social media groups, and bizarrely trying to fish for information, contacted Irene posing as someone else.
When we arrived for our interview, Van den Berg claimed she was sick, but her secretary spilled the beans.
Secretary: She said she told you she’s on sick leave - she was in a zoom orientation that I couldn’t interrupt.
Masa: But she’s working - is she sick or not?
Caught out, Van den Berg called back.
M: When I spoke to you two days ago, you said you knew nothing about complaints against you. Meanwhile, you've got charges that you're facing.
L: That case is sub-judice at the moment. You obviously haven’t followed the case, and there was no evidence that I did any fraud. I was an independent practitioner.
M: By you changing an invoice that was a Procare invoice and going to clients that were Procare clients and making them pay the funds into your personal bank account, that is proof of fraud, Letitia.
L: The court hasn’t found me guilty, and you know that it’s not guilty until found guilty.
M: Some couples, you gave the same baby picture, promised the same baby to multiple couples. You promised babies before they’re even born?
L: I've never guaranteed any people - my last interview I have with every single adoptive parent I tell them, I am not able to guarantee you. My dear, I’m doing this for many years and this is really my passion. I am complying with the act. So, I’m available next week Wednesday, you are more than welcome to come here I will give you my full cooperation.
VO: But it was not to be… on Wednesday morning Van den Berg once again cancelled our interview saying she was hospitalised, so all we’re left with is that she outright denies all the allegations, and claims to have paid back some unhappy clients.
Masa: If you could say something to Letitia right now, what would you say?
Irene: Please don't do it to couples that's been struggling with infertility for so many years. And even if it's just a year, infertility is a terrible journey to be on.


Still holding out for justice, several couples laid charges with the police this week.
